page: Microsoft Azure DC2ds_v3 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the DDCSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a 154 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results indicate moderate single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. The instance achieved average ratings in Geekbench single-core (1664.0) and stress-ng single-core CPU tests (1897.09). However, multi-core benchmarks, such as the Geekbench multi-core score (3005.0) and stress-ng multi-core test (3764.07), fall into the weak category. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large block read-only speeds at 26.16 GB/sec and write speeds at 19.57 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the server demonstrates average performance in single-threaded gzip compression (28.64 GB/sec) and small-model LLM inference, but shows poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (19.64 GB/sec) and weak database operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the DC2ds_v3 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. The inclusion of a 154 GB local disk provides built-in storage capacity without requiring external attachments. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and average single-core performance, this instance is suited for lightweight databases, memory-cached applications, text processing, and basic web serving where multi-core scaling is not a primary requirement.
